correctness.rationale: The four-atom total-variation identity is a direct four-cell calculation. Minkowski gives \(\sqrt A+\sqrt C\ge1\), with equality exactly for constant mixing parameter. Any candidate below target on either diagonal loses to an endpoint product. The remaining convex quadratic projection uniquely fixes \(q_*\). All finitely extendible binary pair laws are convex mixtures of fixed-count urns; distance-to-convex-set convexity reduces worst case to those urns. Their error increases through m<=N/2 by the stated derivative and balanced-pair formula, yielding the even and odd constants. The included standard-library verifier replayed 1,323 urn cases and 9,240 rational-grid candidate comparisons; finite tests do not substitute for these universal proofs.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial finite de Finetti approximation problem receives a complete explicit TV nearest-point formula, proof of unique iid minimizer and an exact parity-sensitive radius for all extension lengths. The closest product often differs from empirical-frequency replacement, and the result supplies a sharp binary benchmark rather than a routine rephrasing of known \(O(1/N)\) bounds. Three-or-more-coordinate and mean-preserving analogues remain unresolved here.
